Quo abiit dilectus tuus, o pulcherrima mulierum? quo declinavit dilectus tuus? et quaeremus eum tecum. »

*Caput ejus.* Modo describit eum secundum humanitatem, modo demonstrat eum secundum alteram partem, id est secundum divinitatem. *Caput ejus,* id est divinitas quae est caput Dominici hominis, est *aurum optimum,* id est divina sapientia Dei optima et perfecta per quam fecit omnia. *Comae ejus,* id [1214C] est illi adhaerentes capiti, subtiles et graciles sunt *sicut elatae,* id est semper tendentes ad superiora. Elatae quidem dicuntur rami palmae qui in summo exeunt, et semper in altum se dirigunt, et ferunt eos triumphatores, et ideo bene comparat eis capillos Christi, qui sunt veri triumphatores, *quae* tales comae sunt *nigrae* id est despicabiles mundo. *Sicut corvus,* id est loquaces et garruli sicut corvus. Vel aliter: Similes corvis, quia natura corvi est ut non pascat pullos donec sint nigri, id est similes sibi. Interim autem resident in ore eorum musculae venientes ad quemdam ipsorum fetorem, et illas devorant, ita sancti nullum pascere volunt cibo spirituali, quem non videant similem sibi, id est diabolo [1214D] renuntiantem, et catholicae fidei obedientem. *Oculi ejus,* id est illi qui subtili intuitu penetrant Scripturas, et aliis praevident. Sunt sicut *columbae super rivos et juxta fluenta plenissima.* Columbae est natura nidificare vel aedificare juxta aquam, ut se reficiat inde, et ut videat ibi umbram milvi vel accipitris, ut possit effugere, ita sancti juxta aquas, id est divinas Scripturas, immorantur, ut inde reficiantur, et ibi sibi praevideant ab insidiis diaboli. Per rivos accipimus minores doctrinas, ut expositiones et sermones sanctorum. Per fluenta plenissima accipimus doctrinam Evangeliorum, ubi plene humana correptio continetur. Columbas dicit lacte lotas, quia fideles illi quos oculos vocat, sunt purgati et mundati *lacte,* id est suavi et dulci doctrina, et [1215A] dilectione Spiritus sancti. *Genae illius,* id est superiores illi sancti qui terunt Scripturas, et inferioribus intelligibiles reddunt, sunt *sicut areolae,* id est terra bene culta et plantata ab ipso Deo. Areolae dico *aromatum,* id est de quibus suavissimi odores orationum et operum praesentantur Deo; et hae areolae, id est hi sancti sunt *consitae a pigmentariis,* id est a sanctis apostolis et prophetis, qui ipsos aedificant doctrina sua et plantant, qui dicuntur pigmentarii, quia terunt omnia reducendo ad humilitatem, sicut pigmentarii species terunt ad pulverem. *Labia ejus,* id est praedicatores per quos loquitur, sunt *distillantia,* id est annuntiantia *myrrham,* id est amaricationes carnis; nullus enim praedicator docet carnem nutriendam. *Primam* dicit, quia [1215B] maxime debet caro mortificari, quia quanto magis caro mortificatur, tanto potius fit robustior spiritus. *Manus ejus,* id est operatores etiam in saecularibus actibus, qui ideo dicuntur manus ejus, quia etiam in his talibus operatur Deus, sunt *tornatiles,* id est planati et suaves, ut in eis Deus non offendatur; sunt *aureae,* id est divina sapientia operantes, sunt etiam *plenae hyacinthis,* id est coelo. Sunt enim boni operatores manuum, intenti prorsus coelestibus, et per divinam sapientiam sciunt operari; per hyacinthum significamus coelum qui est aerii coloris. *Venter ejus,* id est mollior pars Ecclesiae, ut conjugati qui licentius mundo utuntur, sunt *eburnei,* id est casti. Elephas enim frigidae naturae est, unde per ebur castitatem significamus. Ebur enim adeo frigidae [1215C] naturae est, ut superpositus pannus ebori carbone non uratur. Venter dico *distinctus sapphiris,* id est aliquando intentus coelestibus. Oportet enim aliquando conjugatos intendere curis mulierum, aliquando etiam persistere in contemplatione, cujusmodi Apostolus vocat divisos [n: (I Cor. VII)]. Per sapphirum, qui est aerii coloris, accipimus coelum. *Crura illius,* id est illi qui sunt prope novissima tempora, ut illi qui portant eum et annuntiant in his novissimis temporibus, sunt *columnae,* id est sustentatores aliorum, *argenteae,* fulgentes et resonantes nitore divini eloquii, *fundatae super bases aureas,* id est super apostolos et prophetas, qui sunt aurei, quia pleni charitate et sapientia. *Species ejus ut Libani,* quasi dicat: Quid enumerarem [1215D] singula? Species ejus, id est ipse totus, scilicet caput et corpus, sunt ut Libanus, id est candidati et redolentes. *Electus,* id est ipse Christus secundum propriam personam; *ut cedrus,* quia sicut cedrus dignior arbor est inter omnes alias, ita Christus ultra omnes homines est; et ut illa imputribilis est, et odore suo vermes occidit, sic Christus spiritualiter. *Guttur illius,* id est verbum interius, scilicet sensus verborum ipsius, est suavissimus omnibus qui recipiunt. Quid plura? *Totus* est *desiderabilis.* Ecce descripsi vobis qualis esset dilectus meus, filiae Hierusalem, ut et vos ipsi quem talem cognoscitis, fortiter adhaereatis, et mihi de eo debetis credere quia *ipse est amicus meus,* id est mihi familiaris ac bene notus. [1216A] *Quo abiit.* Vox item illorum qui monentur quaerere, et audita qualitate ipsius, quaerunt quasi locum et terram in qua eum quaerant, sicut saeculares amicae sibi invicem loquerentur, et moneret aliqua aliam ut juvaret eam ad quaerendum amicum suum, ut sic dicant: *O pulcherrima mulierum,* id est inter omnes mulieres, id est philosophos, qui dicuntur mulieres, quia nutriunt alios in suis sectis. Pulcherrima dico, indica mihi quo abiit, id est infra quem locum potero eum invenire. Hoc dicit secundum hoc quod est incomprehensibilis, scilicet secundum propriam essentiam ipsius. *Quo declinavit,* dicit secundum haec quae de eo sciri possunt, quasi dicat: Indica mihi qui sunt illi, in quibus habitet Deus, et quibus conferat Deus cognitionem sui, et quare quaerimus, [1216B] quia ecce *quaeremus eum tecum.* Et notatur magna affectio inter eos qui ita se invitant ad inquirendam cognitionem Dei.



## CAPUT VI.

« Dilectus meus descendit in hortum suum ad areolam aromatum, ut ibi pascatur in hortis et lilia colligat. Ego dilecto meo, et dilectus meus mihi, qui pascitur inter lilia. »

*Dilectus meus.* Vox illorum qui invitant alios ad quaerendum Deum, ut sic dicant: Vos quaeritis quo declinavit dilectus meus, et ecce annuntio vobis quia in Ecclesia sua notus est, et ibi habitat, et hoc dicit, *descendit in hortum suum,* id est de cognatione angelorum suppliciter se humiliavit, carnem sumendo, usque ad cognitionem hominum; [1216C] descendit dico *ad areolam,* id est ad illos qui sunt areola, id est qui sunt bene culta terra, et plantata secundum voluntatem Dei. Areola dico *aromatum,* id est illi qui proferunt Deo suavem odorem orationum et operum. Descendit, dico, ad hoc *ut pascatur* et delectetur *in hortis,* id est in fidelibus Ecclesiae suae. *Et lilia colligat,* id est assumat et reponat in secreta sua, *lilia,* id est candidatos in virtutibus, vel colligat et attrahat quosdam in Ecclesia sua quos faciat lilia, id est candidatos omni virtute. *Ego dilecto.* Et mihi iterum de hoc debes credere quia ego dilecto *meo* obsequor in quibus possum, et sum bene ei familiaris, et ideo *dilectus meus* adest *mihi,* praebens auxilium suum et cognitionem suam, *qui* [1216D] pascit et delectatur *inter lilia.*

« Pulchra es, amica mea, suavis et decora sicut Hierusalem, terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata. Averte oculos tuos a me, quia ipsi me avolare fecerunt. Capilli tui sicut grex caprarum, quae apparuerunt de Galaad. Dentes tui sicut greges ovium, quae ascenderunt de lavacro. Omnes gemellis fetibus, et sterilis non est in eis. Sicut cortex mali Punici, sic genae tuae absque occultis tuis. Sexaginta sunt reginae, et octoginta concubinae, et adolescentularum non est numerus. Una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matri suae, electa genitrici suae. Viderunt eam filiae Sion, et beatissimam praedicaverunt reginae, et concubinae laudaverunt eam. »

[1217A]*Pulchra es.* Vox sponsi. Audiens Christus affectionem Ecclesiae, ideo eam commendat cum dicit: *Pulchra es, amica mea,* etc. Pulchram dicit secundum hoc quod habet tantam voluntatem eum cognoscendi; suavem propter hoc quod alios invitat ad idem, non invidens sponsum suum alias habere amicas, decoram dicit secundum opera. *Sicut Hierusalem,* id est ita pulchra sicut Hierusalem coelestis, et decora sicut mater tua, scilicet Ecclesia illa quae te generavit et educavit, *terribilis* inimicis, *ut castrorum acies,* quia in te milito, et tu militas in servitio meo, sicut in castris militatur, et es *ordinata* per institutionem sanctorum. *Averte oculos.* Tu es ita commendabilis, sed tamen desiste putare quod modo credis, ut possis pertingere ad perfectam cognitionem [1217B] mei, et hoc dicit *ante oculos tuos,* id est intelligentiam quam exerces ad cognitionem plenam mei vel oculos ipsos subtilius intuentes, *quia ipsi advolare,* id est separari ab omni cognitione humana, *me fecerunt,* scilicet quia quanto quis subtilius et altius Deum scrutatur, tanto eum altiorem et incomprehensibilem cognoscit. Modo, quia dixit: Averte oculos, ne ista conquereretur se esse indigniorem matre sua, id est Hierusalem, commendat eam sicut fecit superius matrem, cum dicit: *capilli tui,* etc. Dixi: Averte oculos, et tamen habes oculos, etc., aeque pulchra, sicut illa Ecclesia quae te praedicavit. Non ideo dixit ut oculos avertat quod peccatum sit, Deum plene velle cognoscere, sed est peccatum putare posse adipisci. *Sexaginta sunt reginae.* Reginae vel uxores dicuntur omnes illi in sancta Ecclesia, qui [1217C] ex sola dilectione Dei non spe lucri saecularis Deo filios generant; concubinae vero qui non ex dilectione Dei, sed gratia boni temporalis praedicant, et Deo tamen bonos filios generant. Concubinae autem ejiciuntur de domo patrisfamilias, sed filii retinentur. Adolescentulae dicuntur illi qui generantur. Et hoc dicit propter has pulchritudines; habes et reginas et reliquas quae dicuntur sexaginta. Per sexaginta, qui conficitur ex decem et sex, scilicet perfecti in decem praeceptis legis secundum sex opera misericordiae. Per octoginta, qui conficitur ex octo et decem, habemus eos qui, licet decem praecepta aliquantulum custodiant et praedicent, tamen versantur in saecularibus. Octogenarius autem cum in [1217D] malo accipitur, temporalium curas et implicamenta designat, quia et saeculi cursus quatuor circumagitur temporibus, et mundus ipse quatuor climatibus, oriente, occidente, aquilone et austro dirimitur. Concubinae igitur sunt, qui amore temporalium Christum annuntiant. *Una est columba mea.* Cum dicat tot membra Ecclesiae, vellet aliquis discordiam et nunquam unionem inveniri in Ecclesia, et ideo hoc removendo dicit: Quamvis tot partes dixerim Ecclesiae, ipsa tamen una est, id est in fide unitas et est una matri suae, id est ita est una sicut mater sua, id est Ecclesia illa quae istam nutrivit et educavit doctrina suavi. Et est *una genitricis suae,* id est sicut genitrix sua, et sicut praedicatores illi, qui eam converterunt, [1218A] et accipit matrem quantum ad instructionem, genitricem quantum ad conversionem, et quia talis est sicut per omnia supradicta manifestatum est, ideo quaecunque aliae *filiae viderunt eam* admiratae sunt eam, *et reginae et concubinae praedicaverunt* eam *beatissimam* propter gloriam venturam et *laudaverunt eam reginae et concubinae* de virtutibus secundum praesentem vitam.

« Quae est ista quae progreditur quasi aurora consurgens, pulchra ut luna, electa ut sol, terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata? »

*Quae est ista.* Vox Judaeorum qui videntes tantum profectum Ecclesiarum in gentibus, incipientes moveri ad compunctionem, admirantes, non invidentes dicunt: *Quae est ista,* id est qualis et quanta, *quae progreditur [1218B] sicut aurora,* id est per terram diffunditur, sicut aurora *consurgens,* in qua sunt quidam, *ut luna,* id est illuminantes tenebrosos; quidam *ut sol,* id est illuminantes etiam quosdam claros, et sunt quidam in ea terribiles hostibus, quidam sunt *acies castrorum,* scilicet muniti vallo fidei, et ordinati multis virtutibus.

« Descendi in hortum nucum ut viderem poma convallium, et inspicerem si floruisset vinea, et germinassent mala Punica. Nescivi. Anima mea conturbavit me propter quadrigas Aminadab. Revertere, revertere Sunamitis, revertere, revertere, ut intueamur te. »

*Descendi.* Vox sponsi, ut ita respondeat Judaeis: Quaeritis quae sit ista? ipsa quidem est amica mea et hortus in quem ego descendi. *Nucum,* ideo, quia [1218C] in nuce habetur exterius amaritudo, intra testa quaedam fragilis, intus est nucleus dulcis, eodem modo sancti exterius amaricationes multas sustinent intra corpus, quod est testa fragilis; verum intus quidem est dulcissimum, quod est anima ornata multis virtutibus. Descendi dico *ut viderem,* id est probarem et auxilia per gratiam conferrem illis qui sunt *poma,* id est matura opera Deo proferentes, et convalles sunt, id est humiles; *et inspicerem.* Inspicere Dei est gratiam conferre, et fideles probare, *si vineae,* id est hi quibus magnus cultus impenditur, *floruissent,* id est initia virtutum protulissent, *et* si *mala Punica,* id est illi qui paratos se ostendunt cuilibet passioni, *germinassent,* id est aliquem [1218D] fructum Deo acquisissent. *Nescivi.* Vox Judaeorum compunctorum. Dicis quia haec est amica tua, et inspicis eam conferendo ei dona spiritualia; ego quidem nesciebam, quia *anima mea,* id est scientia quam in lege habui secundum carnalem intellectum, *conturbavit me,* id est conturbatum a cognitione Dei reddidit *propter quadrigas Aminadab,* id est propter quatuor Evangelia Christi quae mihi videntur destruere legem, quam prius acceperam. Aminadab interpretatur *spontaneus Domini,* vel *pro populo,* per quem significatur Christus, qui sponte se Deo obtulit, et hoc pro populi redemptione. Per quadrigas quae feruntur quatuor rotis, intelligimus Evangelium quod fertur per totum mundum quatuor evangelistis. [1219A] *Revertere, revertere.* Vox Ecclesiae de gentibus. Cognoscit quidem errorem Judaeorum, commonetque eos ad conversionem. Et ponit quater *revertere,* quia revocat eos de quatuor mundi partibus. Sunamitem vocat eam, id est captivam a diabolo in Babyloniam, id est in confusionem vitiorum. Fuit quidem quaedam Sunamitis captivata in Babylonia. *Revertere* dico, *ut intueamur te,* id est ut in te vitam nostram conspiciamus, vel ut te prae nimia bonitate miremur.



## CAPUT VII.

« Quid videbis in Sunamite, nisi choros castrorum? Quam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calceamentis, filia principis. Junctura femorum tuorum sicut monilia quae fabricata sunt manu artificis. Umbilicus tuus crater tornatilis, nunquam indigens [1219B] poculis. Venter tuus sicut acervus tritici, vallatus liliis. Duo ubera tua sicut duo hinnuli gemelli capreae, collum tuum sicut turris eburnea. Oculi tui sicut piscinae in Hesebon, quae sunt in porta filiae multitudinis. Nasus tuus sicut turris Libani, quae respicit contra Damascum. Caput tuum ut Carmelus, et comae capitis tui sicut purpura regis juncta canalibus. Quam pulchra es et quam decora, charissima, in deliciis! Statura tua assimilata est palmae, et ubera tua botris. »

*Quid videbis.* Vox Christi, et commonet Ecclesiam gentium, ut laboret ad conversionem Judaeorum, quia non erit inutilis labor et praedicatio eorum, quasi dicat: Tu rogas eam ut revertatur, a quo non est cessandum, quia videbis *in Sunamite,* id est in [1219C] Judaeis captivitatis a diabolo *choros,* id est cantantes et psallentes Domino, choros dico *castrorum,* id est in quibus militet Deus, et qui sunt bene muniti. *Quam pulchri!* Item commonet Ecclesia de gentibus ad praedicationem Judaeorum propter aliam causam scilicet, quia multum utile erit et magnum fructum Deo faciet haec novissima Ecclesia in qua erunt Judaei conversi. Non tamen dicitur quod omnes Judaei tandem convertantur, sed major pars. Ideo labora, tu Ecclesia de gentibus, ad conversionem Judaeorum quia valde erunt *pulchri* illi *gressus tui,* id est ultimi fideles qui te et doctrinam tuam portabunt, pulchri dico *in calceamentis,* id est in mortificatione carnis, quia de mortuis animalibus fiunt calceamenta, vel in calceamentis, id est in apostolis et aliis sanctis [1219D] quorum exemplis et auctoritate protegentur ultimi, sicut pedes calceamentis. *Filia principis,* id est Dei Vel potest hic esse vox Christi ad ipsos Judaeos per apostrophen. *Junctura femorum,* id est coadunatio duorum populorum, *sicut monilia* quia muniunt et monent quidem alios, ut considerantes suam pulchritudinem et dona spiritualia quae in ipsis vigent, velint sibi adhaerere; muniunt vero subditos contra insidias diaboli, et docent eos castitatem. Monilia dico *fabricata* potentia et operatione summi *artificis,* id est Dei ipsius.

*Umbilicus tuus.* In hac parte ventris mulier habet seminarium generationis, et per hanc partem, quae est in ventre, habemus illos qui cum sint inter carnales, [1220A] ut conjugati, habent tamen seminarium praedicandi et generandi Deo filios. Et hi tales sunt *crater,* id est potans et inebrians alios Dei dilectione. Crater dico *tornatilis,* id est ita planatus secundum voluntatem Dei, ubi manus Dei nullam inveniat offensam, qui crater, *nunquam,* indiget *poculis,* quia hujusmodi sanctis nunquam deficiet doctrina qua potent alios. Vel umbilicus ideo dicuntur hujusmodi sancti praedicatores, quia sicut umbilicus est in medio ventris, ita isti sunt in medio populi concionantes et reconciliantes eos Deo. *Venter tuus,* id est illa mollior pars Ecclesiae, qui alios non generant, *sicut acervus tritici vallatus liliis.* Acervus ideo dicit, quia multi sunt tales in Ecclesia. Tritici dicit, quia et tales sunt suavis cibus et delectabilis [1220B] Dei, et sunt vallati, id est bene muniti *liliis,* id est in virtutibus. *Duo ubera,* id est praedicatores, qui sunt ubera, scilicet vasa lactis, id est doctrinae suaviter educantis. Hi tales sunt *hinnuli,* quia leves et agiles ad currendum, non praegravati pondere carnis, *gemelli* dicit, quia sicut gemelli fratres, licet sint diversi, tamen sibi similes, ita hi duo populi Judaeorum et gentilium sibi similes erunt, quia eamdem instructionem legis et sequentur et docebunt *capreae* quia capreae virtutes habebunt. *Collum tuum,* id est, illi qui in Ecclesia novissima officium colli habebunt, erunt *sicut turris* quia ad eos confugientes defensionem invenient, *eburnea* dicit propter castitatem. *Oculi tui,* id est, illi sancti praevisores et subtiliter Scripturarum profunditatem intuentes, [1220C] sunt *sicut piscinae,* id est aquae reficientes doctrina verbi Dei omnes sitientes. *In Hesebon,* quod inter pretatur *cingulum moeroris,* sunt sancti illi qui sunt oculi et aquae dicuntur, et in Hesebon, quia semper cincti sunt moerore et propriorum et aliorum delictorum, quae piscinae, id est doctrinae sunt *in porta,* id est parati ad refectionem *filiae multitudinis,* id est multorum filiorum. Sunt enim quasi in porta, quia omnibus qui accedere volunt parati sunt ut eos spirituali aqua reficiant. *Nasus tuus.* In naso continetur discretio boni ac mali odoris, et per hoc significantur illi qui habent discretionem bonorum et malorum, ut discernant qui sint bonae voluntatis, et eos instruant, et qui sint simulatores et dolosi, et eos rejiciant. Hi tales sunt *turris Libani,* turris, quia [1220D] fugientibus sunt opportuna munitio, Libani, quoniam candidati sunt virtutibus. Vel turris, quia sicut turris fortis est munitio, ita sancti in discretione sua non vincuntur, quia fortes, sicut in electione sua nec falluntur, ut bonum judicent malum, vel malum bonum, *quae respicit contra Damascum.* Fuit quidem Damascus contraria semper Hierusalem, et cives suos invicem subtrahebant, et interpretatur Damascus *potus sanguinis,* per quam significantur persecutores sanguinolenti qui persecutionem inserunt vel gaudent in malis aliorum, contra quos respiciunt praedicti sancti, ut aliquos cives istis subtrahant, et in corpus suum traducant. *Caput tuum,* id est mens tua, vel altiores in Ecclesia, sunt, *ut [1221A] Carmelus,* id est habentes scientiam circumcisionis. Intelligunt enim per praeputium amputatum, ubi est sedes libidinis, et per quod generatio tota succedit, amputandam a nobis omnem veterem generationem, scilicet depositionem omnium sordium, quae tandem perfecta erit in communi resurrectione. Carmelus interpretatur *scientia circumcisionis. Et comae capitis,* id est illi qui proxime adhaerent capiti Ecclesiae, scilicet veri pauperes qui Christo proxime adhaerent, sunt etiam quasi ornamentum ipsius capitis. Hi tales sunt *sicut purpura regis,* id est imitatores passionis Christi, qui verus rex est, purpura dico *vincta canalibus,* id est passio eorum sit juncta et dependens a canalibus, id est a cogitationibus et cordibus, scilicet ut cum proponant se imitatores passionis Christi, [1221B] non sit hoc secundum exteriora tantum, sed etiam secundum interiora. Dicuntur canales vasa illa in quibus tinguntur purpurae, et sicut purpura si bene adhaereat canali melius tingitur, ita isti passioni Christi melius adaptantur, si per exteriora et interiora se compassibiles ostendant. *Quam pulchra.* Quid per singula? *Tota pulchra es,* secundum interiores virtutes, *et decora* secundum opera, *in deliciis,* id est in omni spirituali refectione. *Statura,* id est directio *tua* sicut palmae. Sicut enim palma in altum semper fertur, ita fideles isti semper tendunt ad altitudinem virtutum, *et ubera tua,* id est, doctrinae tuae similes sunt *botris,* id est vino, sicut enim vinum, ita doctrinae tuae inebriant.

« Dixi: Ascendam in palmam, et apprehendam fructus ejus. Et erunt ubera tua sicut botri vineae, et odor oris tui sicut odor malorum. Guttur tuum sicut vinum optimum, dignum dilecto meo ad potandum, labiisque et dentibus illius ad ruminandum. Ego dilecto meo, et ad me conversio ejus. Veni, dilecte mi, egrediamur in agrum, commoremur in villis. Mane surgamus ad vineas, videamus si floruit vinea, si flores fructus parturiunt, si floruerunt mala Punica. Ibi dabo tibi ubera mea. Mandragorae dederunt odorem suum in portis nostris. Omnia poma nova et vetera, dilecte mi, servavi tibi. »



## CAPUT VII. (cont.)

*Dixi: Ascendam.* Ponit aliam causam quare Ecclesia de gentibus praedicare debeat Judaeis, ut si ita diceret: Tu praedicare debes quia utilis erit praedicatio [1221D] tua, et multi convertentur, tum quia conversi tales et tam probi erunt, sicut dictum est, tum quia ego ipse veni proprie eos redimere, unde dictum est, Matth. XV: « Non sum missus nisi ad oves quae perierunt domus Israel, » et hoc dicit, *Dixi,* id est ab aeterno disposui, *ascendam in palmam,* id est in crucem, in qua dicitur quaedam pars fuisse de illa arbore, vel in palmam quia ibi obtinuit victoriam diaboli, et de obtentu mundi triumphavit, Dixi ascendam *et apprehendam fructus ejus,* id est generabunt mihi filios, et proferent bonas operationes. Modo convertit se ad eam sponsus ipse, cum dicit, *et ubera tua,* id est doctrinae tuae *sicut botri* non hederae, sed *vineae,* id est et dulces ad bibendum, [1222A] et inebriantes aliquos qui diligenter eos audiunt, *et odores tui,* id est fama et devotio tuorum *sicut* odores *malorum;* sicut enim poma odore suo aliquos attrahunt, ita isti etiam fama sua sibi aliquos attrahunt et sociant. Erunt quidem valde boni illi ultimi Judaeorum, sicut ostendit Apostolus qui dicit, Rom. II: « Et si diminutio eorum divitiae sunt gentium, quanto magis plenitudo eorum? » Licet enim non omnes convertantur, tamen major pars eorum convertetur. *Guttur,* id est verba interiora, scilicet sensus verborum tuorum, est *sicut vinum optimum,* id est nutrientia et inebriantia homines, ut faciant oblivisci totius vitae suae prioris. *Dignum dilecto.* Vox Ecclesiae, et commendat verba illa quae etiam tam digna sunt ut ea Christus a Deo Patre accepisset, [1222B] ut ita dicatur: Dico tuum guttur sicut vinum optimum, et adeo optimum ut sit *dignum dilecto meo,* id est Christo *ad potandum,* id est ut Christus ea potet, id est sine labore, et cum delectatione *labiis,* id est praedicatoribus, *et dentibus,* id est fortioribus, qui Scripturas conterunt dignum *ad ruminandum,* id est dignum ut labia et dentes ruminent, scilicet terant et laborent ad intelligendum. *Ego dilecto meo,* quasi dicat: Mihi credendum est, quia ego adsum ei semper familiaris ex conscientia secretorum, et ipse me diligit, et hoc dicit: *Ad me conversio ejus,* id est ad me amorem suum convertit. *Veni, dilecte.* Modo Ecclesia, audita commonitione Christi, parataque ad praedicandum Judaeis, invitat sponsum ut secum sit in praedicatione illa auxilium sibi conferens, quasi dicat: Praecepisti mihi praedicare Judaeis, quod nihil proderit sine auxilio tui, et ideo, *dilecte mi, veni,* id est aspira eos interius, *et egrediamur,* id est, extra gentes gradiamur *in agrum,* id est ad praedicationem illorum qui sine magno labore faciunt fructum, et *commoremur in villis,* id est in aedificatione et ordinatione ipsorum. *Mane surgamus,* id est studiose laboremus; qui enim studiosi sunt, mane surgunt ad opera sua. Per vineas accipimus illos in quibus laboratur antequam fructum reddant, et *videamus si vineae,* id est illi tanto labore exculti, *floruissent,* id est, initia virtutum emisissent, *si flores,* id est, illi in quibus jam apparent initia virtutum *fructum,* id est, matura opera, *parturiunt,* et videamus *si mala Punica,* [1222D] id est futuri martyres adhuc *floruissent.* Dixi: Veni, dilecte, ad quos quidem mecum debes venire, quia *ibi dabo tibi,* id est ad tuum honorem *ubera mea,* id est doctrinam meam qua tibi optimos acquiram filios. *Mandragorae.* Dico quia ibi dabo tibi ubera mea, quod bene potero facere, quia ipsi Judaei jam dederunt mihi bonam opinionem suae conversionis, scilicet idoneos se exhibentes ad recipiendam fidem. Mandragorae sunt herbae, et habent similitudinem cum humanis membris absque capite; per quod significantur Judaei carentes capite, id est Christo. Per portas intelligimus fidem, quia est porta, et introitus omnibus ad salutem. *Omnia poma.* Dixi quod darem tibi ubera mea, quod vere faciam, quia *servavi [1223A] tibi,* id est ad honorem tui, sententias Novi ac Veteris Testamenti, quibus tibi aliquos fructus faciam, quae sententiae, et suaviter sunt redolentes, et audientes ita dulciter attrahunt sicut poma.



## CAPUT VIII.

« Quis mihi det te fratrem meum sugentem ubera matris meae, ut inveniam te solum foris et deosculer te, et jam me nemo despiciat? Apprehendam te et ducam in domum matris meae, et in cubiculum genitricis meae. Ibi me docebis, et dabo tibi poculum ex vino condito, et mustum malorum granatorum meorum. Laeva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me. »

*Quis mihi.* Hic ostenditur effectus praedicationis Ecclesiae quia loquuntur Judaei audientes sibi annuntiandum [1223B] Christum, et accensi amore ipsius prorumpunt in haec verba, *Quis mihi det,* id est utinam aliquis mihi annuntiet *fratrem meum,* id est Christum de carne mea natum *sugentem ubera matris,* id est educatum doctrina Synagogae. Modo ex nimio amore convertit se ad ipsum. Quis mihi det dico *ut te inveniam foris,* id est, ut hominem te cognoscam in quo turpiter erravi, *et deosculer te,* id est delecter in agnita tua humanitate *et jam me nemo* despicabilem putabit, qui prius fui contemptui omnibus. *Apprehendam te,* id est, qui prius fueramus a te separati modo tibi firmiter adhaerebimus. Apprehendam dico, et ducam in domum matris meae, id est illos qui modo serviunt Synagogae, Christo faciam servire, et *in cubiculum genitricis meae,* id [1223C] est quosdam de Synagoga tales efficiam in quibus cubet ac quiescat sine offensa Deus. *Ibi,* id est dum te filiis Synagogae annuntiabo, *me docebis,* quia ego aperiam os, et tu illud adimplebis sicut promisisti [n: (Psal. LXXX)], *et dabo tibi poculum,* id est convertam tibi multos de Judaeis qui erunt tibi poculum, id est delectabilis potus, et refectio per bona opera sua, et in multis virtutibus. Cujusmodi potum sitit Deus, ut ipse dixit in cruce, « Sitio [n: (Joan. XIX)], » scilicet traduco in corpus meum genus humanum. Poculum dico *ex vino condito,* id est quod poculum sit vinum, id est viri calentes amore Dei, et alios inebriantes dilectione Dei. Quod vinum est conditum, id est confectum multis speciebus, id est virtutibus diversis [1223D] ipsorum sanctorum, et dabo etiam poculum, *mustum* scilicet vinum calidum, fervens ac bulliens, per quod significantur sancti martyres ferventes ad amorem martyrii, qui etiam dicuntur mala granata, quia exterius rubei propter passionem, interius candidi propter virtutem. *Laeva ejus,* et bene debeo laborare ut tales sibi acquiram, quia ipse mihi confert solatium, et per temporalia, et per spem aeternorum.

« Ajuro vos, filiae Hierusalem, ne suscitetis neque evigilare faciatis dilectam donec ipsa velit. Quae est ista quae ascendit de deserto, deliciis affluens, innixa super dilectum suum? Sub arbore malo suscitavi te. Ibi corrupta est mater tua, ibi violata est genitrix tua. Pone me ut signaculum [1224A] super cor tuum, ut signaculum super brachium tuum, quia fortis est ut mors dilectio, dura sicut infernus aemulatio. »

*Adjuro vos.* Vox sponsi. Audiens namque Christus tantam affectionem Ecclesiae Judaeorum, commendat eam sicut et superiores. et praecipit subditis ne eam inquietent. *Quae est ista.* Vox Ecclesiae de gentibus. Videns namque filiam suam Ecclesiam de Judaeis ad tantam perfectionem pervenisse, gaudens non invidens, cum admiratione dicit, *Quae est ista quae ascendit.* Per gradus virtutum, *de deserto,* et infidelitate sua, in qua erat deserta a Deo, *affluens deliciis,* id est abundans multis virtutibus *innixa super dilectum suum,* id est Christum quem habet fundamentum omnis recte incedens. *Sub arbore malo.* Vox Christi [1224B] ad Ecclesiam illam de Judaeis modo conversam, et commendat eis dilectionem suam. Conveniens namque erat ut, cum liber iste totus sit de dilectione Dei, in fine sui tractatus commendaret dilectionem. Continuatio. Innixa est Ecclesia de Judaeis super me dilectum suum. *Pone* igitur, tu Ecclesia de Judaeis, *me super cor tuum,* id est regentem cor tuum et cogitationes tuas. Et aliter, *super,* id est compressorem totius iniquitatis tuae, pone dico *ut signaculum,* id est ut pateat amicis te continere mea secreta, et inimicis item pateat te non esse de eorum secta, vel ab eis secreta quae habes esse clausa et ignota. Vel signaculum, scilicet ita me pone ut teneas in corde imaginem mei, scilicet disponas te similem mihi et in passione et in omnibus aliis pro tuo modo, et pone [1224C] me *super brachium tuum,* id est operationem tuam, ut me rectorem habeas in omnibus operibus tuis. Pone dico, *ut signaculum,* id est ut per ipsa opera pateat amicis te esse familiarem mihi, ac de consortio eorum inimici te intelligant alienam a vita et moribus eorum, et quod hoc debeant facere, praemissa est causa, cum dictum est: *Sub arbore malo,* quasi dicat: Merito debes me ponere super cor tuum, quia mortuam in peccatis liberavi te et hoc dicit, te jacentem et languidam *sub arbore,* id est sub peccato facto per arborem *malo,* id est in peccato primi parentis. Vel, languidam, sub peccato crucis quae item fuit de arbore hac, id est malo. Legitur enim in libris Graecorum quod de eadem [1224D] arbore in qua peccavit Adam, ramus quidam aliatus fuit Hierosolymam, et ibi plantatus excrevit in magnam arborem, de qua postea facta sit crux Domini, ut ex quo mors venerat eodem vita repararetur. Dicitur quoque Adam in eodem loco sepultus, in quo postea fixa fuit crux Domini; *ibi,* id est in arbore illa *corrupta fuit et violata mater,* id est Synagoga. Per corruptam notat peccati poenam in quacunque, in sententia, qua ex crucifixione Domini habuerunt Judaei poenam, scilicet destructionem illam quam intulerunt eis Titus et Vespasianus. Cum dicit violatam, notat aeternam damnationem quam ex peccato illo habuerunt omnes qui non resipuerunt. Continuatur et aliter versus iste sic: Dixit Ecclesia me dilectum suum, et merito debes me diligere, quia [1225A] ego liberavi te a peccato primi parentis. *Quia fortis est.* Videlicet ideo debes me ponere super cor tuum, quia dilectio mea fortis est sicut *mors.* Sicut enim mors non potest impediri quin veniat, ita dilectio Dei non potest aliqua persecutione impediri quin salvationem faciat, ut deducit Paulus [n: (Rom. VIII)]. Vel sicut mors destruit corporeos sensus, ita dilectio Dei. Qui enim dilectione Dei bene occupatus est, jam non trahit ex visu aliquam delectationem carnis, nec ex caeteris sensibus. Vel sicut mors, id est, ipse diabolus qui est causa totius mortis. Sicut enim diabolus suis inimicibiliter damnationem confert, ita dilectio Dei salvationem. *Aemulatio,* id est affectus dilectionis, scilicet efficere ea quae dilectio, exigit sunt cura et importabilia carni; *sicut infernus,* [1225B] id est insatiabilis est illa aemulatio. Nulli enim in quo abundat dilectio, videtur satis sua dare vel caetera facere quae exigit dilectio, imo semper vellet plus facere.

« Lampades ejus lampades ignis atque flammarum. Aquae multae non potuerunt exstinguere charitatem, nec flumina obruent illam. Si dederit homo omnem substantiam domus suae pro dilectione, quasi nihil despiciet eam. »

*Lampades ejus.* Item describit naturam illius dilectionis, quasi dicat: Ad illam dilectionem festinare debetis, quia *lampades ejus,* id est ardores hujus dilectionis, sunt sicut *lampades ignis,* id est ardores sancti Spiritus, et hoc est quod dicit, *ignis.* Sicut enim ignis calorem ministrat, ita Spiritus sanctus [1225C] aestum dilectionis, et quia posset esse ignis qui non luceret, dicit *ac flammarum,* id est tales sunt lampades dilectionis quod etiam luceant, scilicet illi qui habent has dilectiones lucent aliis, quia alios illuminant verbo et exemplo. Possumus etiam per lampades accipere homines illos in quibus habitat dilectio sicut in lampade ignis. *Aquae multae.* Ostendit iterum aliam naturam dilectionis ut et nos amplecti ipsam velimus, ut ita dicatur: Talis est dilectio. Hanc vero dilectionem neque minae neque persecutiones parvae vel magnae poterunt exstinguere. Per aquam accipimus minas et hujusmodi parvas tribulationes, quia exstinguunt humanos amores. Per flumina habemus majores adversitates. *Si dederit [1225D] homo.* Item commendat dilectionem hanc, ut fortiter nos invitet ad eam conservandam, cum dicit esse talem hanc, pro qua si det aliquis *omnem substantiam,* id est universam possessionem suam, et super seipsum despicit eam, id est despicabilem judicabit ad comparationem quam obtinebit.

« Soror nostra parvula, et ubera non habet. Quid faciemus sorori nostrae in die quando alloquenda est? Si murus est, aedificemus super eum propugnacula argentea. Si ostium est, compingamus illud tabulis cedrinis. »

*Soror nostra,* dicit sponsus. Lex dilectionis tam gravis est, sed soror, id est Ecclesia de Judaeis quae dicitur soror Christi, quia et de eadem carne, et cohaeres regni cum. Christo, ut noviter conversa est, [1226A] *parvula* adhuc tenera in fide *et ubera,* id est doctrinam *non habet* ex se, et ideo nisi auxilium ei praebeamus, legem dilectionis ferre non poterit. *Quid faciemus?* Dicit sponsus ad amicos suos: Quia soror nostra adhuc parvula est, oportet ut conferamus auxilia ei, et *quid faciemus ei in die quando alloquenda est?* In hoc praesenti tempore in quo instituenda et alloquenda est ut post hanc vitam digna inveniatur, quae Christo copuletur in nuptiis. Quid faciemus, dico hoc scilicet *si murus est,* id est si aliqui sunt in hac Ecclesia qui sint murus et defensio aliorum. *Aedificemus super eum propugnacula argentea,* id est sententias quibus sciant se defendere et alios impugnare, et haec *argentea,* id est tinnientia compositione eloquii, scilicet sapientes et eloquentes [1226B] faciamus eos. *Si ostium est,* id est si aliqui sunt in hac Ecclesia introducentes, *compingamus illud,* id est aliquid apponamus quod sit eis ad honorem, compingamus, dico *tabulis,* id est tales adjungamus qui sint tabulae, id est subtiles et bene dotati ad voluntatem Christi, ut isti tales sint auxilio eis qui sunt ostium. Tabulis dico *cedrinis,* id est tales adjungantur qui sint cedrini, id est imputrescibiles, et odore suo vermes occidentes.

« Ego murus et ubera mea sicut turris, ex quo facta sum coram eo quasi pacem reperiens. Vinea fuit Pacifico in ea quae habet populos. Tradidit eam custodibus, vir affert pro fructu ejus mille argenteos. Vinea mea coram me est. Mille tui Pacifici, et ducenti his qui custodiunt fructus [1226C] ejus. »



## CAPUT VIII. (cont.)

*Ego murus.* Vox Ecclesiae Judaeorum, proferentis perfectionem suam, ut ita dicat: Dicis; Si murus est, aedificemus. Ego quidem murum habeo, id est quidam sunt in me qui sunt murus et aliorum defensio, et sunt in me *ubera,* id est doctores sancti qui sunt *sicut turris* inexpugnabiles et invincibiles in doctrinis suis. Dico quia hoc habeo et ex eo tempore *ex quo facta sum coram te,* id est in bene placito tuo *quasi pacem reperiens,* quae prius discordiam per peccatum habueram. *Vinea fuit.* Ostendit Ecclesia de Judaeis quod ipsa debeat in Christo pacem reperire, quia Ecclesia de gentibus quae nullum Dei cultum receperat, pacem cum Deo reperit [1226D] et hoc dicit: *Vinea,* id est Ecclesia de gentibus in cujus cultu maxime laborandum *fuit Pacifico,* id est pacem invenit cum Deo. *In ea,* supple pace, *quae habet populos,* id est in qua pace sunt multi cum Deo gentilium, dico quia vinea fuit Pacifico, et propter hoc *tradidit eam custodibus,* id est ordinavit in ea pastores, et doctores, vel angelicos custodes, cujus Ecclesiae tanta dignitas est ut ille qui vir vult esse, id est viriliter agere afferat dividendo convenienter *mille argenteos,* id est omnia quae de mundo habet, afferat dico et praesentet Deo *pro fructu ejus,* id est pro vita aeterna quae est fructus Ecclesiae. *Vinea mea.* Vox sponsi. Dixisti quia Ecclesia de gentibus mihi esset in pace, non solum ea placet mihi, sed universa *vinea mea,* id est omnis Ecclesia [1227A] tam de Judaeis quam de gentibus *coram me est,* id est in bene placito meo semper existit. *Mille tui Pacifici,* id est omnium simul oblata possessio coram me est. *His autem qui custodiunt fructus ejus* ut sancti pastores qui provident, ne sancti subditi amittant fructus aeternitatis, sunt *ducenti* argentei, id est duplex pretium. Ducenti enim duplex est ad centum. Custodes autem sanctae Ecclesiae duplex pretium Deo offerunt, quia et se immaculatos Deo observant, et alios lucrantur, et ideo duplici praemio remunerantur.

« Quae habitas in hortis, amici auscultant te, fac audire vocem tuam. Fuge, dilecte mi, et assimilare capreae hinnuloque cervorum super montes aromatum. »

[1227B]*Quae habitas in hortis.* Quia sponsus modo Ecclesiae dixerat: Vinea mea coram me, et caetera talia, ne Ecclesia putaret statim assumi ad nuptias, praemonet eam ut iterum, dum non assumitur, laboret et operetur, ut bene parata nuptiis copuletur et hoc dicit: Tu sponsa quae nondum duceris in thalamum, [1228A] sed adhuc habitas in hortis; unusquisque enim fidelium habitat in hortis, id est in Ecclesia, *fac me audire,* id est dignam te effice auditui meo, et habes per quos perferas mihi tam orationes quam opera, ut mihi placent, amicos meos, et hoc est quod dicit, *amici auscultant,* id est parati sunt ut bona opera tua Deo praesentent. Ad hoc quidem fiunt litaniae in Ecclesia, ut per sanctorum intercessionem Dominum placidum invenire mereamur. *Fuge, dilecte mi,* quia me oportet habitare in hortis, nec possum adhuc sociari tibi in thalamo sic sicut vis, id est sustineo mihi abesse praesentiam corporis tui. Hoc autem rogo ut condescendas nobis et cognitionem tuam non solum perfectis, sed per ipsos ostende inferioribus. Et hoc dicit. *Assimilare [1228B] capreae hinnuloque cervorum,* scilicet descende in colles ut videaris ab humilibus. Tu dico habitans *super montes,* id est villis altioribus qui sunt eminentes in virtutibus. Montes dico *aromatum,* id est de quibus profertur Deo odor virtutum ac bonae operationis.

## Expositions on the Song of Songs

[1187A]At the beginnings of books the reasons must be stated, how and why the book itself was composed — reasons which Jerome calls the prooemium. The author, then, of this work of which we intend to treat had three names: he who, to the number of his names, composed three books, and distinguished their purpose by the interpretation of the names themselves. In the first book, then, tenderly and sweetly, after the manner of a father lovingly admonishing his son and, as it were, offering him milk, he instructs each of the faithful who is as yet less strong and not yet willing to renounce earthly things altogether. In which book, on account of this great sweetness, he is named Idida, which means *beloved*. For in it he teaches that the harlot must be fled, and the fellowship of the wicked, and the other things worthy to be done with honor and uprightness — one, however, as we have said, still [1187B] dwelling in the world. His second name is Coeleth, which in Greek is called *ecclesiastes*, in Latin *concionator*. Now we call that man a preacher who in the assembly of men, that is in the council, is a public orator, fearing no one in the utterance of truth, flattering no one: which this man does in his second book. For, as if by certain steps of ascent — in order to bring to perfection the one whom he would draw by his teaching, to whom first, mercifully yet lawfully, he had granted the use of these earthly things together with works of mercy (since he believed that a carnal and still weak mind could not hold heavenly and more perfect things) — now, as though [he were] stronger and able to take up higher things, he invites him in this second book to the contempt of all earthly things; and he shows how fleeting and how transitory [1187C] are all temporal things, saying thus: *Vanity of vanities, and all is vanity [n: (Eccle. I, 2)]*. This indeed pertains to the contemplative [life] — namely, to despise all worldly things and to gape after heavenly ones; but that which had been granted in the first book, to the active life. Moreover, for the sake of what thing he would urge [one] to undertake so great a labor, he shows in this his third book, to those who attend spiritually, by certain earthly similitudes — to this end indeed, that through the contempt of earthly things we might be able to attain to the glory [1188A] of eternal things. In which work he is called Solomon, that is, *the peaceable one*.

This book is called the Song of Songs, and that too in the plural, on account of the great excellence of its dignity. For Solomon first made parables, namely the book of Proverbs, in which he plainly shows how we should rightly use these worldly things; which pertains to the active life, and can be called simply a Song. Now Proverbs are called precepts concerning human life [given] through certain similitudes. Then he made Ecclesiastes, in which he announced that all worldly things are to be despised, as when he says: *All* things are *vanity*; and it is a certain step from the active to the contemplative, and can be called simply a song. After these he made this book, in which he teaches concerning the love of God, as though [1188B] the world had already been despised: which pertains to the contemplative life; hence it is called the Song of Songs, namely a song more excellent than the two aforesaid, and than the other like ones. The name of this book in Hebrew is *Sir hasirim*, which among us amounts to *the Song of Songs*. Solomon is said, according to these three books which he made, to have had thirty names: according to the parables he is called Idida, that is, *beloved*: for there, instructing the untaught, he began to be loved by them: by which name Christ is signified, who by excellence is called beloved: of whom God [says]: *This is my beloved Son [n: (Matth. XVII)]*. Ecclesiastes is the name both of the book and of the author, and is interpreted *preacher*, namely one making diverse people consent to the same thing. For diverse people are called together in that book that they may consent among themselves in the contempt of the world: which [1188C] is drawn from the similitude of a singer, who governs the voices of diverse people into one harmony. Likewise by this name Christ is signified, who is the true preacher, teaching that earthly, transitory things are to be spurned, and heavenly ones to be loved. He is also called Ecclesiastes, because he excellently governs the Church and calls it together to one faith. According to this book he is called Solomon, that is, *the peaceable one*, by which likewise he signifies Christ, who is the true peaceable one and calls all together to the love of himself. [1189A] The author is also called, in Proverbs, an ethicist, that is, one treating of morals. The same [is called], in Ecclesiastes, a physicist, that is, one treating of the nature of things. In the Song, a theologian, discoursing of divine things. In this book the subject-matter is the bridegroom and the bride, the friends of the bridegroom (who are also called paranymphs), and the friends of the bride. Now the bridegroom is God, since he pledges himself to the Church; namely, that if she keep faith with him, not committing fornication with the demon, he will at last join her to himself in marriage. The bride is said to be the Church, namely those firm in the faith, since, perfectly receiving the faith, she pledges herself to God and renounces the pomps of Satan. The friends of the bridegroom are said to be, as it were, the holy angels and the more perfect, such as the apostles, who help the bridegroom to retain his beloved, admonishing and helping the Church, that she may not commit fornication with a stranger, but cleave to God alone [1189B]. The friends of the bride are said to be those still tender in the faith, who do not fully know how to love the Bridegroom, but already show themselves apt to imitate the bride, so that, being thus well instructed by the bride, they too may become the bride. Now he treats of this subject-matter in this manner: showing how in this life the bridegroom addresses his beloved, both by himself and through his friends, and with how great affection she receives the words of the bridegroom, and how the friends of the bride show themselves ready to imitate the bride, and how they speak to the bride, and sometimes to the Bridegroom himself. For Solomon, still holding the gift of wisdom, illumined by the Holy Spirit, prophesies how the Church, before the coming of Christ, and thereafter according to her several states down to the end of the world, will conduct herself toward God. The end and purpose too is that he may impel his hearers to the love [1189C] of God. Now this author writes like a comic poet, namely saying nothing in his own person, but bringing in the very characters speaking: and because in no [other] love are words of love found so tender as between bridegroom and bride, he makes them speak, as it were, in the words of carnal love. And these are the first words of the Church now close to the coming of Christ, and now, with exceeding love, desiring his presence; like those who said: Do you think I shall see [it]? Do you think I shall last? Do you think that Nativity will find me? And as a carnal bride, to whom the bridegroom had already pleased exceedingly through messengers, now disdaining the envoys, longing for his presence, would say: Let him come himself, that being present he may speak with me and kiss me — so here those faithful just before Christ say:



## CHAPTER ONE.

[1189D] « Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth, for thy breasts are better than wine, fragrant with the best ointments; thy name is oil poured out, therefore the maidens have loved thee. »

God himself, as he was foretold through the patriarchs and through the prophets, this same one now — *let him kiss me*, that is, let him now delight me *with the kiss*, that is, with the presence, *of his mouth*, that is, of his Son, who is called the mouth of the Father just as also the Word, because through him the Father is made manifest to the world. *For thy breasts are better.* Here the Church now present speaks with Christ. As though she should say thus, turning herself to him out of exceeding affection: For *thy breasts*, the evangelical teaching, *are better than wine*; which teaching is a sweet refreshment and pleasant like milk. It is better than [1190A] *wine*, that is, than the teaching of the philosophers, which does not nourish but intoxicates, and makes those who receive it grow proud, and leads at last to destruction. Or by wine let us understand the carnal understanding of the Old Testament. We can also by the breasts understand the twofold love, or the two Testaments spiritually understood, or spiritual graces; and yet the meaning will be the same as the aforesaid. The breasts, I say, are *fragrant*, that is, sweet-smelling, and drawing men to themselves by their odor. For that teaching gives off a sweet smell, and draws to itself by its good repute and fame; *with the best ointments*, that is, through the best ointments. For in the evangelical teaching there are ointments, that is, spiritual gifts which are the best, compared to the carnal ointments with which lovers used to be anointed, that they might please the better — or also those dining. Now these [1190B] ointments are rightly called the best: for those whom they anoint they make true kings and priests. *Oil poured out.* Another reason why she had desired him: because *thy name* is poured out, like oil poured out. Oil indeed, while it is in the vessel, neither gives forth odor nor heals pains; but poured out it both emits odor and heals pains: so the name of God, while he was still held enclosed in the bosom of the Father, was little or not at all known: but after he took flesh, visiting the world by his presence, he set himself forth to be known by all; he sent forth an odor, that is, fame and good repute of himself: and, poured in, through the sufferings of those who well received his preaching, he healed [their] sins as well. *Therefore the maidens*, namely, because thou art so worthy and so sweet, therefore not only I, but also the [1190C] *maidens*, that is, the lesser and more fragile, still tender in the faith, *have loved thee*, that is, out of all things they have chosen thee alone as the one to be loved. For although they still take consolation for themselves from temporal things, yet they judge that God is to be preferred to those temporal things.

## THE VOICE OF THE CHURCH.

« Draw me after thee: we will run in the odor of thy ointments. The king has brought me into his storerooms. We will exult and rejoice in thee, mindful of thy breasts above wine. The upright love thee. »

*Draw me after thee.* The contemporaries of Christ, seeing that his ascension, as it were, now threatens, and the absence of his consolation, ask him to draw them after himself, that is, to make them his imitators. And he fittingly says *draw*, as if by a certain violence. For violence seems [1190D] to be done, where a body born in sins is freed from sins. *We will run in the odor.* The voice of the friends of the bride. Hearing the goodness of the Bridegroom, and that the greater ones wish to become his imitators, they say to the bride, namely to their teachers, having now tasted the sweetness of God: Thou wilt go after him, and we too will surely run with thee, that is, we will labor with thee to obtain the joy of the marriage, placed and founded *in the odor*, that is, in thy preaching and fame, which draws us, which is [the odor] *of thy ointments*, that is, proceeding from the spiritual gifts through which thou workest. She rightly says *we will run*, for not by being slothful and acting sluggishly shall we attain to that heavenly prize. *The king has brought me in.* The voice of the Church to the lesser ones whom she has raised. Hearing indeed that they [1191A] desire God, they wish to invite them to the same, as if those greater ones should answer thus: You say that you will run with me; and one must run well, because for those who arrive there is the highest refreshment. And she shows that this lies open to her when she says: *The king has brought me*, that is, he has given manifest knowledge, *into his storerooms*, that is, into the secret things of the Church, namely that I may know what the mysteries signify — as that in baptism the Spirit is given, that infants are saved by grace alone, and the like, which do not lie open to all. Or by the storerooms let us understand the fullness of blessedness, that is, the eternity of life, just as in storerooms a great abundance of goods is wont to be laid up; and perfect men are, in hope, already brought into the blessedness of eternity. *We will exult.* The voice of the lesser ones who, having advanced somewhat through faith, now dare to speak to the Bridegroom in these words: [1191B] Because thou, Lord, hast already brought thy bride into thy secret places, therefore we too will prepare ourselves as fit, that we may be brought in with her: and this is *we will exult*, namely in the body, that is, we will work well with exultation, *and we will rejoice* in soul, because in gladness we will think good things. Or *we will rejoice*, namely, if we do good things, not compelled but willingly: and this *in thee*, that is, we will attribute all things to thee as to the first cause, from which every good radically proceeds; and this we will do *mindful of thy breasts*, that is, of thy sweet teaching, *above wine*, as was said above. *The upright love thee*, namely, we ought well to exult in thee and to love thee, because all who are upright do this; wherefore, unless we do this, we cannot be upright. The end is plain in all the aforesaid, because [1191C] whether we wish to imitate the more perfect or the lesser, by their words we are invited to the love of God.



## THE VOICE OF THE CHURCH AGAIN.

« I am black, but beautiful, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the skins of Solomon. Do not consider that I am dark, because the sun has discolored me. The sons of my mother have fought against me: they set me as keeper in the vineyards; my own vineyard I have not kept. Show me, O thou whom my soul loves, where thou feedest, where thou liest down at noon, lest I begin to wander after the flocks of thy companions. »

*I am black.* The voice of the bride to the lesser ones. For the bride, hearing the promise of the lesser ones that they would run with her, fearing lest they fail in persecution — [1191D] inasmuch as these had as yet tasted nothing but the love of God alone, and reckon the saints as madmen, because they are held contemptible in the world — forewarns them not to consider the evils, namely so as to desist for this reason from their promise, but to attend to what rewards they may obtain for the persecution, so that she says in this manner: You say that you will run with me, but then you must be blackened in the body, just as I, on account of many tribulations, am black outwardly. And she puts the effect for the cause. Outwardly indeed I am black, *but* inwardly *beautiful*, that is, adorned with good virtues, I say to you, *O daughters of Jerusalem*, that is, whom I have begotten to the faith, you who also now see peace. Now these lesser ones are called daughters because they are of the fragile sex, and can quickly be deceived and called away from the faith; and because greater guardianship [1192A] and care is to be applied to them than to sons, namely the stronger ones; and because these, when confirmed, beget others — I say that I am black *like the tents of Kedar*, that is, like Kedar dwelling in tents. Kedar was a son of Ishmael, as is said in Genesis XXV and I Paralipomenon I, but so wicked that he was received by no one in the house, but always dwelt in tents; of whom Origen [says]: « His hand against all, and the hand of all against him. » *I am black like Kedar*, beautiful like *the skins of Solomon*. The skins indeed in which Solomon dwelt were well stripped of hair, and dyed red, adorned with various paintings; so holy men are stripped of all superfluity, and are adorned with many kinds of virtues. He rightly compares the saints to skins, because as a skin is called the hide of a dead animal, so the saints, mortifying [1192B] themselves, become, as it were, simply skins. And he rightly added *of Solomon*, since these skins, namely the saints, are that tabernacle in which the true peaceable one does his warfare.

*Do not consider.* I say that I am black, but do not attend to this, so as to desist for this reason from what has been begun: *because the sun*, that is Christ, who is the true brightness, *has discolored me*; namely, for his sake I have suffered all these things, who will at last be able to reward me. *The sons of my mother.* She shows through what ministers of his God so proved her in persecutions, namely through the sons of my mother, who first begot me in carnality. She ought to have been to me a spiritual mother, and to nourish me with the milk of divine understanding. These my brothers *fought against me* with diverse kinds [1192C] of persecutions: and thus, by persecuting, *they set me as keeper in the vineyards*, that is, in the churches of the Gentiles. *My own vineyard*, that is, the vineyard which by nature I ought to have cultivated and kept, *I have not kept*. Here we note that state of the Church when the apostles transferred themselves from Judea to the Gentiles, as the apostle Paul says in Acts XIII: Because you have rejected us, and shown yourselves unworthy of the word of God, behold, we turn to the Gentiles. *Show me.* The voice of the Church of those who, Judea being dismissed, now begins to build among the Gentiles; and here she prays to God not herself, but in the person of those who are newly converted: and here she prays to God, that he may give them knowledge of himself, namely that they may know in whom God dwells so that they may imitate them; and that they may also know who [1192D] are heretics so that they may not follow them; so that she says thus: I am set as keeper in the vineyards, and that I may be able to keep them, and thence present fruit to thee, *show me*, that is, to these new ones — which is surely to thy honor — *where thou feedest*, that is, in whose working thou art refreshed; or *where thou feedest*, that is, to whom thou offerest food, namely thy body or the refreshment of the divine word. Show me also *where thou liest down*, that is, restest, namely where no offense may disturb thee, *at noon*, that is, in the splendor of thy majesty, or in the fervor of charity: namely those who are not in the evening, so that love should now grow cold in them, nor in the morning, so that it should be only tender in them. Show, I say, thou *whom my soul loves*, that is, the whole affection of my mind; and she adds the reason why she prays this, *lest I begin*, that is, therefore I pray that thou show me, [1193A] lest I begin — that is, lest these of the Gentiles, still new in the faith, begin *to wander* and to hold to byways *after the flocks of thy companions*, that is, by imitating the heretics, who are called the companions of Christ, because, that they may the better deceive, they preach something of the truth, agreeing with Christ, but are diverse by inserting heresies among it. But if they agreed in all things, they would be called not companions, but, as it were, the very same. Or companions because they themselves call themselves his companions and friends. He rightly says flocks because they are both many and without true reason.

« If thou knowest not thyself, O fairest among women, go forth and depart after the footsteps of the flocks, and feed thy kids beside the tents of the shepherds. To my cavalry among the chariots of Pharaoh have I likened thee, my beloved. Beautiful are thy cheeks like [those] of a turtledove, thy neck [1193B] like necklaces. We will make thee little chains of gold, inlaid with silver. »



## THE CHURCH.

« While the king was in his repose, my nard gave forth its odor. A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me; he shall abide between my breasts. A cluster of Cyprus is my beloved to me, in the vineyards of Engaddi. »

*If thou knowest not thyself.* The voice of the bridegroom. And here he does three things: he threatens, he coaxes the bride, and he also sets forth the means by which the Church may be able to obtain knowledge of herself. The connection. Dost thou seek knowledge of me? For which it is necessary for thee, *O fair one* — [fair] in virtues and in my choosing — that thou know thyself, namely thy dignity which I gave thee through faith, and by giving thee my body and blood, [1193C] and moreover the other spiritual gifts; because if thou knowest not thyself, in what dignity thou art from this, that thou art my bride, *go forth* from the fellowship of the Church, *and depart*, that is, be made far from the Church, so that thou even lose the virtues which thou hadst before. Depart, I say, *after the footsteps*, that is, by imitating the works, *of the flocks, and* thus *feed the kids*, that is, take delight in thy foul acts, and let them be food for thee; and this, *beside the tents of the shepherds*, by imitating those who call themselves shepherds and warriors for God in tents, and are not, but are heretics; or beside the tents of the true shepherds, and not within. For the heretics wish to draw the authority for their uncleannesses from the Holy Scriptures in which holy men do warfare for God — as certain men called Nicolaitans, whose heresy is condemned, Apocalypse II; and [condemned] by the Church in it. *But certain heretics* [1193D], 24, q. 3, who preach that women are to be held in common, and say that the Apostle said all things are to be held in common, and other things of this kind. *To my cavalry.* Having set down the threats, he sets down blandishments, as if he should say: If thou knowest not thyself, go forth; but thou oughtest not to go forth or to be ignorant of thyself, because I have so honored thee as to make thee my beloved, and to free thee from Egypt; which was prefigured in the liberation of the children of Israel from Egypt, Exodus XII. Now the Gentile world is led out of Egypt, that is, out of the darkness of unbelief, and out of the power of Pharaoh, that is, out of the yoke of the devil, through the Red Sea, because through baptism, where all the enemies are submerged, that is, all sins; and this he says, *I have likened thee to a cavalry*, that is, to that in which I did warfare, going among the chariots, [1194A] that is, among the chariots, or in the time of the chariots of Pharaoh. By the chariots in which the powerful sat is denoted the pride or the fickleness of this world. *Beautiful are thy cheeks.* Having set down threats and blandishments, he shows that there are in her means by which she might retain knowledge of herself. I said, if thou knowest not, go forth — which thou needest not do, because thou hast cheeks and a neck by which thou canst hold true knowledge. The cheeks are called that part of men which grinds food and sends it into the belly: so in the Church the higher ones are called cheeks, those who grind the Scriptures and make the lower ones capable of them; and as in the cheeks there is a sign of modesty, so they always preach modesty and chastity — which cheeks are *beautiful*, namely with many virtues, and are *like [those] of a turtledove*, because as the turtledove never has [1194B] but one mate, nor sings except by moaning, so these have Christ alone as bridegroom, and moan very often for their own faults and those of others. The office of the neck is that through it the ground food may descend into the belly, and that it may hold the body to the head; by which are signified the disciples of those higher ones, as Timothy was to Paul, through whom the Scriptures descend to the lower ones, and these by their preaching join the Church to Christ. *The neck*, I say, being *like necklaces*. A necklace warns some where they may take refuge, and protects the breast of the one wearing it, lest anyone lay hands on it; so these by their teaching both protect the Church, lest the adulterer devil lay hands on her, and warn the lesser ones of the Church where they may take refuge and whom they may follow. *Little chains of gold.* The voice of the friends of the bridegroom. Wishing to help the bridegroom, [1194C] as to how the Church may remain in the knowledge of herself, they say: The bridegroom gives thee cheeks and a neck, and we will give the ornaments of the ears. If the same ones who are the cheeks or the neck speak these things, it does no harm. A muraenula (little chain) is named from the muraena (moray), which coils itself into a circle; and by the murenae we signify rounded and perfect sentences, with which the saints adorn the inner ear, that is, the understanding; *of gold*, that is, seasoned with divine wisdom and charity, *inlaid with silver*, that is, distinguished with the best eloquence. Or the sentences and the wisdom which they have in themselves they know how to dispense to each one by honorable arrangements according to his measure — to the wise, as they are, to the humble likewise. Silver, which is a metal that rings better than the others, and by it eloquence is signified. And this we will do [1194D] while the king is in [his] repose, that is, in the confession of God, namely bodily removed from the Church; or this is carried over to what follows: *While the king was.* The voice of the Church answering thus: The bridegroom and his friends give me such ornaments, and therefore *my beloved [is] to me*, that is, to my honor, *he shall abide between my breasts*, that is, in my inmost love; and the cause is put first, as if she should say: Rightly ought I to love him, because he himself gave me nard, namely virtues, and this while he was *in his repose*, that is, in his passion, [in his] resurrection — namely because he himself suffered and rose again, and from this he gave me virtues which gave forth *their odor*, that is, [an odor] befitting them, to wit, good fame. Or, *while the king was in his repose*, that [1195A] is, because he chose the tranquillity of my mind in which to dwell, therefore *my nard gave forth its odor*. Nard is an ointment made from a lowly herb, and the herb itself is likewise called nard, by which humility is signified; and it is of a hot nature, by which charity is signified. The beloved, I say, *shall abide between the breasts*, and he himself will be to me both great sorrow and great joy — namely, for all the adversities which he himself suffered I shall grieve, and for those by which he was not burdened, I shall rejoice; and this he says: *A bundle of myrrh*. By myrrh is denoted bitterness, because it is a most bitter thing, and therefore bodies anointed with it remain whole, because on account of its great bitterness the worms do not approach. By the bundle is denoted a multitude of bitternesses. Likewise *my beloved shall be to me a cluster [1195B] of Cyprus*, that is, a great joy. By the cluster we have wine, in which is gladness. Cyprus is a place in which the best wine grows. The Church rejoices together with the bridegroom, as over the resurrection and the like. I said « my beloved shall abide between my breasts, » and this *in the vineyards of Engaddi*, that is, in the churches, where there is a fountain of the kid, because there the foul are washed in baptism, and become white. Now Engaddi is interpreted *fountain of the kid*, or *temptation of the eyes*. Now the Church is set in the temptation of the eyes in this world, in which all things are set before us for the tempting of the eyes.

« Behold, thou art beautiful, my beloved, behold, thou art beautiful, thy eyes [are those] of doves. »



## THE VOICE OF THE CHURCH.

« Behold, thou art beautiful, my beloved, and comely; our bed [1195C] is flowering, the beams of our houses are of cedar, our panels of cypress. »

*Behold, thou art beautiful.* The voice of the bridegroom, hearing toward himself so great an affection of the bride, in that she had said: « My beloved shall abide between my breasts, » answers her:

Because I abide with thee with so great love, « behold, thou art beautiful. » Which he sets down twice: note that she is beautiful both in body and in soul. *Thy eyes [are those] of doves*, that is, dove-like, namely gazing simply, and lacking gall and envy.

*Thy eyes*, that is, thy preachers, who provide for thee as the eyes for the body, shall be *of doves*. It is said intransitively, that is, they shall truly be doves, that is, having the seven virtues, which are denoted by the seven natures of the dove. For the dove dwells beside the streams, [1195D] so that, when a hawk is seen, it may plunge and escape; it chooses the better grains, it nourishes another's young, it does not tear with its beak, it lacks gall, it nests in the caverns of the rock, it has moaning for song. So the holy preachers dwell beside the streams of Holy Scripture, by which their hearts are watered, so that by their protection they may escape from the diabolical assault. The better grains, that is, the better sentences, namely not those of the heretics, they choose. Another's young, that is, men, at first estranged from Christ, who had been young ones, that is, sons of the devil, they nourish by their teaching and example. They do not tear with the beak, that is, they do not pervert good sentences by tearing them in the manner of the heretics. They lack gall, that is, they lack irrational anger. They nest in the caverns of the rock, that is, in the wounds [1196A] of the death of Christ, who is the most firm rock, they place their nest, that is, in faith in the death of Christ they place refuge, or hope. For by the nest refuge and hope are designated. For the dove, when rain comes on, flees to the nest, and has its hope in the nest. It has moaning for song, that is, as others take delight in song, so they [take delight] in tribulation and moaning. The dove has also this nature, that it recovers lost sight; so also the preachers and provisors of the Church, when some gift of the Holy Spirit has been lost through some fault, recover it, like David, who recovered the spirit of prophecy which he had lost. It has likewise this nature, that it flies in flocks. In the same way the preachers, in flocks, that is, holding the catholic faith, strive toward the heights by the steps of good works and virtues. For [1196B] as many good works as we do, by so many steps do we hasten to God. The dove defends itself with its wings; so good preachers protect and defend themselves with the sentences of the Fathers.

*Behold, thou.* The voice of the bride. Thou, O bridegroom, callest me beautiful, and such I must be because thou art beautiful, and therefore, unless I were beautiful, I could not be joined to thee. *Beautiful* is said according to [his] divinity, *comely* according to [his] humanity. *The bed*: the bridegroom is beautiful, and the bride beautiful, and therefore their coverings are beautiful. By the bed we have those in whom God [dwells], because, to whatever small degree he rests in those in whom he himself rests, the Church is not offended, but rests. Now such [persons] are flowering, that is, having the beginnings of good works. By the flower, therefore, we understand the beginning, since [1196C] the flower precedes the fruit. *The beams of the houses*: by the beams we understand those strong ones who bear the weight of the Church, who are of cedar. The cedar is a tree that does not rot, and by its odor kills the worms; so these, since they have eternity now at least in hope, both by their preaching and their good fame kill the vices in the hearts of others. *The panels* are things hanging from the beams, and are ornaments of the house, and by this are signified those who, hanging from the more perfect, adorn the Church by good instruction and by fame, who are of cypress. The same [is meant] of the cypress as was said of the cedar. When he says *of your houses*, he gives us to understand that Church of the Gentiles, now somewhat grown up.

## CHAPTER II.

## THE VOICE OF CHRIST.

[1196D] « I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys. As the lily among thorns, so is my beloved among the daughters. »

## THE VOICE OF THE CHURCH.

« As the apple tree among the trees of the woods, so is my beloved among the sons. Under the shadow of him whom I had desired I sat, and his fruit was sweet to my throat. The king brought me into the wine cellar, he set charity in order within me. Support me with flowers, surround me with apples, because I languish with love. His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me. »

*I am the flower.* The voice of the bridegroom, and he stirs the Church to endure the passion, and sets himself before them as an example, because without his own necessity he endured many things, as if he should say: I have called thee beautiful, and thou art [so], *like the lily [1197A] among thorns*. For as thorns, moved by the wind, tear the lily and pierce it, so the daughters, that is, those given over to the softnesses of the world, agitated by the inspiration of the devil, rend the holy Church; nor oughtest thou to flee, but rather be a lily, because I, when I had no need, was a lily — that is, I was the flower of the field, and I was a lily, namely pricked by many persecutions; I indeed who was a lily so as to be pricked, was also a lily, that is, the glory of the valleys, that is, of the humble. Christ is rightly compared to a flower, because as a flower is born of itself, and is the glory of the field, so Christ, born without human seed, was the glory of the Church and of the whole world. *As the apple tree.* The voice of the Church saying thus: My beloved admonishes me to the passion, and I am ready to obey him, relying on his support, who is *like the apple tree*. As the apple tree draws travelers, [1197B] both by the odor of its fruit and by its good shade, and then by the refreshment of its fruit, more than the other trees, so Christ [draws] both by the odor of good working and by the shade, that is, protection, which he confers by spiritual gifts, and by the fruit, that is, the Eucharist, better than anyone of all. And thence she adds: *Under his shadow I sat*, that is, in his protection against the heat of the devil they rest; *his fruit*, that is, his body and blood, or the refreshment of the divine word, is sweet *to my throat*, that is, to my heart. Besides these things also *the king brought me*, namely he who is able to sustain and defend me in every tribulation, *into the cellar*, into a certain gathering of the Gentiles, which is enclosed by faith and works like a cellar — thus he multiplied the Church; he says *wine-cellar*, because the Church serves wine, that is, the love of God [1197C] with which those who drink are inebriated, so much that they forget their kindred and their former life. With these things *he set charity in order within me*, that is, he arranged charity in me by order, namely that in the first place, according to dignity, I should love God, and him with all my strength, then my neighbor, and this in diverse degrees. In the first place, [my] father; last of all, [my] enemy, and this for the sake of God. Now charity is founded in us in this order, that we should first love ourselves, and afterward our neighbor, that is, that the same nature which we wish to be saved in ourselves, we should wish to be saved everywhere; and because we love our own nature, we are led to the love of the Creator of this nature, and so the love of God, which is held the worthier, is held later in time. Whence John: « If anyone does not love his brother whom he sees, how can he love God [1197D] whom he does not see? [n: (I Joan. IV.)] » And because he has done these things for me, therefore *I languish* with love of him, that is, I afflict myself even to the failing of the flesh; and because I so languish, therefore *support me*, that is, bring me consolation from the initiated and the perfect. By the flowers, the beginnings; by the apples, the ripe works, namely of the perfect. For the consolations of the saints are the good works of others. *His left hand.* Solomon says in Proverbs III: « Length of days is in his right hand, and in his left hand riches and glory, » and so here we understand by the left, or the sinister [hand], temporal things; by the right, eternal things. And thence the bride says: « I languish with love of him, » but he will not desert me, because « his left hand, » that is, these temporal things, are *under my head*, that is, under my mind, because [1198A] my mind despises these things, and yet is sustained by them; for it could not keep watch and do the other things of this kind, if the body were not refreshed by them. The left hand, I say, [is] under [my] head, *and his right hand*, that is, eternity, will at last receive me — [that eternity] which now I hold by hope alone. As the left hand is less worthy than the right, so are temporal things than eternal.

## CHRIST.

« I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes and the harts of the fields, that you stir not up, nor make to awake, the beloved, until she herself will. »



## THE CHURCH.

« The voice of my beloved: Behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, bounding over the hills. My beloved is like a roe and a young hart. Behold, he himself stands behind our wall, looking through the windows, gazing [1198B] through the lattices; and my beloved speaks to me: Arise, prosper, my beloved, my dove, my beautiful one, and come. For now the winter has passed, the shadow has gone and departed; the flowers have appeared in our land, the time of pruning has come. The voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land, the fig tree has put forth its green figs, the flowering vines have given their odor. Arise, my beloved, my fair one, and come, my dove, in the holes of the rock, in the caverns of the wall. Show me thy face, let thy voice sound in my ears. For thy voice is sweet, and thy face comely. »

*I adjure you.* The voice of the bridegroom. Seeing his beloved languish with love of him, and now persist wholly in tranquillity of mind and in contemplation, he commands the lesser ones [1198C] and subjects not to move her away from that rest by sins and disobediences: as if he should say thus: because my beloved languishes with love of me, therefore *I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem*, that is, you who are begotten in the vision of peace, *by the roes and the harts of the fields*, that is, if you wish to have the natures of the roe and the hart, which the saints have. The nature of the roe is to seek the heights, to be of clear sight — whence it is called dorcas, that is, seeing clearly; to choose clean pastures; if it be pierced through by an arrow it knows how to heal itself — so the saints both seek the height of the virtues, and gaze upon the Scriptures clearly and subtly, and are refreshed by the clean pasture of the divine word, and if they are wounded by some arrow of the devil, they cure themselves by penance and prayer, running to Christ, who, as though he were dittany, casts the iron out of the wounded.
